evidence.claim: IFF's 2025 business included Taste, Food Ingredients, Health & Biosciences, Scent, and Pharma Solutions until divestiture; Taste products are used in food and beverage categories, Scent products are used in household and personal care products, and the former Pharma Solutions segment included pharmaceutical excipients.

Sensient describes itself as a global manufacturer and marketer of colors, flavors, and fragrances, with products including specialty food and beverage systems, cosmetic and pharmaceutical ingredient systems, and other specialty chemicals.
Sensient's 2024 fact sheet reported revenue across Flavors & Extracts, Color Group, and Asia Pacific, supporting that the company has material exposure to specialty flavor and color systems.

Balchem's Human Nutrition and Health segment provides human-grade choline nutrients and mineral amino acid chelated products for nutrition and health applications; its annual report states sales growth relies partly on differentiation through scientific data, intellectual property, and customer factors.

Balchem states that its Human Nutrition and Health business offers nutrition and sensory solutions, while the company identifies itself as a global leader in choline production and encapsulation technology.

Innospec's personal-care portfolio includes surfactants, silicones, antibacterial agents, emollients, solvents, conditioning agents, rheology modifiers, actives, emulsifiers, and other ingredients for beauty and personal-care formulations.
Innospec's home-care business offers surfactants, additives, and high-performance formulations used in cleaning, laundry, dish-care, and household products.

The node-level bottleneck logic is that API and regulated-input suppliers can become sticky because switching a qualified source may require regulatory revalidation, filings, inspections, and long waiting periods; this evidence was provided in the external search context and is used as a general analogy rather than a company-specific fact.

The key chokepoint test for this node is not headline consumer demand alone but whether ingredients are qualified inside customer formulations, regulatory files, plant audits, IP-protected systems, or sensory/performance specifications that slow supplier switching.
Next pass should search for US-listed food-safety, QC testing, excipient, and private-label OTC input suppliers that are smaller than $10B and not classified as obvious consumer companies.

node: Regulated specialty inputs for consumer health, staples, beauty, nutrition, and private-label products
summary: Layer 1B expands the regulated-specialty-inputs node into a two-lane US-listed universe. The reference lane uses IFF as a visible flavor/fragrance/nutrition benchmark. The underfollowed lane focuses on mid-cap suppliers whose products are embedded inside consumer food, beverage, personal care, home care, nutraceutical, pharmaceutical, or OTC formulations. The chokepoint hypothesis is that approved ingredients, formulation know-how, customer qualification, regulatory files, and plant-quality systems may create higher switching costs than generic chemical or ingredient labels imply.
